Amanda W: Hey team, a customer hitting our /v1/rerank/batch endpoint says returned scores are misaligned with per-query candidate lists. They sent two queries with different candidate counts and results appear shifted across queries :confused:
Samir K: Ugh. Do we have the raw request + response?
Amanda W: Pasting sanitized request/response they provided. Note: they replace IDs with x's.
Amanda W: ```json
POST /v1/rerank/batch
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "candidates": ["A", "B", "C"]},
    {"id": "q2", "candidates": ["D", "E"]}
  ]
}
```
Amanda W: Response they got:```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q1", "scores": [0.2, 0.3, 0.1]},
    {"query_id": "q2", "scores": [0.9, 0.4, 0.05]}
  ]
}
```
Amanda W: Notice q2 has 3 scores even though it had 2 candidates — and the top scoring item (0.9) actually corresponds to candidate A from q1 when validated against a local rerank model.
Samir K: That looks like an off-by-one/flattening bug where we write back a single scores buffer but don't respect per-query lengths when slicing. Has anyone seen similar? :eyes:
Devon R: I saw a ticket months ago about batch offsets in the runtime; we patched one path but maybe some client-facing path still uses the old serializer. Tagging @Rita for oncall.
Rita (oncall): On it. Can you attach request-id / sample headers and approximate time? Need prod log trace.
Amanda W: They included headers: X-Request-ID: xxxx-1111; Timestamp: 2027-05-08T14:03:12Z. Customer tenant id: org_78x. I grabbed a chunk from our logs: `rerank.batch: request_id=xxxx-1111 num_queries=2 total_candidates=5 serialized_len=5`
Lee M: Hmm serialized_len=5 is correct, but we should be tracking per_query_candidate_counts = [3,2]. If the response loop uses a global cursor and a stale per-query length array, we could be slicing wrong. I'll check the marshalling code in runner/serialize.py line ~220.
Samir K: Also, did they hit any 4xx/5xx? They said 200 but wrong scores. We should check if there was any partial fallback to approximate scorer.
Amanda W: They confirm 200 OK and results returned quickly (low latency). Customer is pretty annoyed since top suggestions were dramatically wrong for q2.
Devon R: Repro attempt: I made a local curl to our staging with their body and got expected alignment. So might be data-dependent or specific to that model variant (rtr-v2-quant).
Amanda W: They said model=rtr-v2-quant in the request.
Samir K: Good catch. Lee, can you try reproducing against rtr-v2-quant with the exact shapes/quantization flags? I'll search commits for any batching change touching quantized path.
Lee M: Reproduced locally with rtr-v2-quant and a randomized candidate set; if I force batch size >1 I sometimes see the extra-score leak. Looks like in quantized_executor we used `memcpy` offsets but the offsets array wasn't updated when compacting candidates for identical tokens. Code snippet:```c
// quantized executor copy loop
for (i=0; i < total_candidates; ++i) {
  memcpy(output + offsets[i], scores_buf + i, sizeof(float));
}
```
Lee M: offsets array was built from per_query_counts but if there was a candidate dedup step that removed entries earlier, offsets got out of sync. Fix idea: rebuild offsets after dedup/compression step.
Rita (oncall): Can we push a short-lived hotfix to staging and run customer's exact payload? If that passes we can prepare a prod patch with a migration note.
Amanda W: Customer is asking for repro steps to confirm on their side — they can run the same request again if we want, but prefer we validate first.
Samir K: I'll open an internal bug with repro attached and mark P1 for incorrect semantics. Also add a regression test covering varied per-query candidate lengths and dedup-path.
Samir K: Created issue RED-2386 with logs + minimal repro. @Lee can you attach your failing test case to the ticket?
Lee M: Done, pushed branch fix/quant-offset-rebuild and test. Running CI now.
incidents-bot: Deployed staging build `canary-2027-05-08-09` to staging cluster in us-west-2 :rocket:
Devon R: CI green for unit tests, but want a quick e2e on staging with the customer's exact request to be safe. I can trigger it.
Rita (oncall): After e2e pass, we should reach out to the customer with a short explanation + ETA for prod patch. Also offer rollback if anything else breaks.
Amanda W: I'll message the customer with the plan: validate on staging then schedule prod patch within 24h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Samir K: Postmortem action: add fuzz tests for multi-query/batch serializers and a monitoring alert for response length mismatches (response.scores_count != request.candidates_count sum).
Amanda W: Adding that to the support playbook so CS can quickly collect headers/ids next time.
Rita (oncall): FYI I took ownership of prod deploy once QA signs off.
Amanda W: Closing loop here when patch is live.
